candidate.mechanism: An onset-aligned adservice CPU runaway or saturation condition, potentially caused by an internal compute loop or resource leak; the available metrics do not distinguish this from a CPU-instrumentation anomaly.

candidate.service: shared inter-service communication path affecting emailservice, paymentservice, shippingservice, and checkoutservice
candidate.mechanism: A shared dependency or network/inter-service latency condition began at the incident onset, increasing RPC response times across multiple services while CPU, memory, workload, error logs, timeout logs, and trace status codes did not show a corresponding service-local failure. This is the leading working theory, not a verified root cause.
A cartservice-side connection/socket-resource condition may have increased failed frontend requests, with frontend request errors appearing as the user-visible symptom.

A sharp increase in ts-travel-service CPU utilization coincided with and plausibly drove elevated travel-service and downstream request latency, consistent with CPU saturation or a compute-intensive regression in the travel service.

A restart or termination of ts-auth-service at approximately 1733834342 interrupted authentication traffic; the service then required roughly 55 seconds to initialize before serving requests again. The initiating cause of the restart is not established.

A sharp incident-boundary increase in adservice CPU utilization may indicate localized CPU saturation or an injected adservice resource fault, but the available evidence does not establish that it caused the reported incident.

A post-onset latency condition in checkoutservice causes roughly 200 ms delay across checkout-related spans; serial dependency calls then accumulate into multi-second PlaceOrder latency and the observed checkoutservice p50/p90 increase.

A cartservice RedisCartStore.AddItemAsync path attempts to parse a stored value outside the Int32 range with Int32.Parse, raises OverflowException, returns FailedPrecondition, and propagates request errors to frontend.

A resource or execution-pressure condition affecting ts-travel-service caused a large CPU increase, which coincided with materially increased travel-service p90 latency and propagated latency to dependent services. The evidence is broad-window and observational, so this is a medium-confidence working hypothesis rather than a verified root cause.

A ts-auth-service runtime/resource degradation, reflected by a post-onset CPU increase from 4.45% to 16.07%, memory increase from approximately 229.5 MB to 429.1 MB, socket increase from 10.29 to 15.25, and markedly prolonged login/token traces, appears to be the most likely proximal cause. The evidence does not establish whether the underlying mechanism is a memory leak, thread/connection contention, request amplification, or another application-level condition.
